label: Task 2 discuss both views
question: Some people believe that university students should study whatever they like. Others believe they should only be allowed to study subjects that will be useful in the future, such as those related to science and technology. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
essay:
Choosing a subject at university is one of the most important decisions in a young person's life. While some argue that students should be free to follow their interests, others believe that only practical subjects such as science and technology should be offered. This essay will discuss both views before explaining why I believe students should have freedom of choice.

On the one hand, there are clear reasons to focus on science and technology. These fields drive economic growth and create well-paid jobs, so graduates in engineering or computer science are less likely to be unemployed. Moreover, governments usually fund universities with public money, so it seems reasonable for them to want graduates who can solve national problems such as climate change or the shortage of doctors. For instance, many Asian countries have invested heavily in engineering faculties and this has helped their industries to grow rapidly.

On the other hand, limiting students to useful subjects ignore the value of the arts and humanities. Subjects like history, literature and philosophy develop critical thinking and communication skills, which employers in every industry are looking for. In addition, students who study something they are passionate about tends to work harder and achieve better results. If a talented musician was forced to study chemistry, society would lose a creative person and gain an unmotivated chemist.

In my opinion, students should be allowed to choose any subject, but universities should give them clear information about career prospects. This way, young people can make an informed decision while society still benefits from a wide range of skills.

In conclusion, although science and technology are important for the economy, I believe freedom of choice leads to more motivated graduates and a more balanced society.

label: Task 2 advantages and disadvantages
question: More and more people are choosing to work from home rather than in an office. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages? Write at least 250 words.
essay:
Over the past decade, and particularly since the pandemic, remote work has shifted from a rare privilege to a mainstream arrangement. Although working from home can leave some employees isolated and blur the line between professional and personal life, I would argue that its benefits, for both workers and society, are considerably greater.

The most immediate advantage is the time and money saved on commuting. In congested cities such as Bangkok or London, a daily round trip can easily exceed two hours, and eliminating it gives employees more time to rest, exercise or spend with their families. This, in turn, tends to improve wellbeing and reduce burnout. Remote work also widens access to employment: parents with young children, people with disabilities and those living far from economic centres can compete for jobs that were previously out of reach. On a broader scale, fewer cars on the road means lower emissions and less pressure on public transport at peak hours.

Admittedly, these gains come at a cost. Without the casual conversations of an office, employees may feel lonely, and junior staff in particular can miss out on the informal mentoring that helps them develop. There is also a risk that, with a laptop always within reach, the working day never truly ends. However, these problems are largely manageable. Many companies now adopt hybrid models, bringing teams together one or two days a week for collaboration and training, while clear policies on working hours can protect employees from being permanently available.

In conclusion, while remote work presents genuine challenges related to isolation and work-life balance, these can be mitigated through sensible management, whereas its advantages in time, wellbeing and accessibility are substantial. On balance, therefore, the advantages clearly outweigh the drawbacks.

label: Task 1 Academic table
question: The table below shows the percentage of households with internet access in four countries in 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2020. Country A: 30, 52, 74, 91. Country B: 45, 60, 71, 80. Country C: 12, 25, 48, 77. Country D: 60, 68, 72, 75. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
essay:
The table shows the percentage of homes that had internet access in four countries between 2005 and 2020.

Overall, internet access increased in all four countries over the period, but the speed of growth was very different. Country C grew the most, while Country D changed only a little.

In 2005, Country D had the highest percentage with 60%, followed by Country B at 45% and Country A at 30%. Country C had only 12% of households online, which was the lowest. By 2010, Country A had risen to 52% and Country C doubled to 25%.

In the following years the growth of Country A and Country C continued strongly. Country A reached 91% in 2020, which was the highest of all countries. Country C also increased dramatically to 77%. On the other hand, Country B and Country D grew more slowly and in 2020 they were 80% and 75% respectively, so Country D went from the first place to the last place.

label: Task 1 General Training complaint letter
question: You recently bought a piece of equipment for your kitchen, but it did not work. You phoned the shop but no action was taken. Write a letter to the shop manager. In your letter: describe the problem with the equipment; explain what happened when you phoned the shop; say what you would like the manager to do. Write at least 150 words. Begin your letter: Dear Sir or Madam,
essay:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a coffee machine which I bought from your shop on 3 March. Unfortunately, it has not worked properly since the first day.

When I switched the machine on, the light came on but no water came through, and after a few minutes it started to make a loud noise. I followed every step in the instruction book, but the problem did not disappear.

On 5 March I telephoned your customer service department and explained the problem to a member of staff. She told me that a technician would call me back within two days to arrange a repair. However, nobody has contacted me since then, although I called again last week and was promised the same thing.

I would therefore like you to replace the machine with a new one or give me a full refund. I have kept the receipt and the original box. I would be grateful if you could reply within seven days.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Kim
